bootstrap.resampled: source groups within each task, the mix weights applied afterwards

units.table_v1_and_v2: figures/pareto.json, figures/pareto_tasks.json and figures/table_v2.json hold tables v1 and v2, unchanged; the figure JSONs also hold G's steps and operating points under `jev` and G+'s under `jev_bolstered`, as E's are under `rules`, the plotted numbers of chart v3
units.operating_points: G's and G+'s operating points per mix and quality target, keyed by the router's letter: the rows table v1 gives a router (the same ones as figures/pareto.json's), each the cheapest certified step of the walk (Amendment A9, items 9 and 10). Costs include Jev's overhead on every routed request (A15 item 10); a point that falls back to A is A itself, with no router call and no overhead
units.comparisons: descriptive, with no multiplicity correction: at 95%, about one interval in twenty excludes 0 by chance
units.same_target: keyed by `first less second`, then mix, then quality target: the first router's operating point less the second's, paired over the same resamples. cost_per_1k: dollars per 1,000 requests; quality: 0 to 1 under the mix. Each is value, low, high (percentile 95%), `undefined` 0. Where either side falls back to A, that side is A; where both do, `reading` says "both fall back to A" and both estimates are null. G against F-train is not made: G uses no labels (A15 item 14)
units.matched_cost: per router, mix and target: the envelope's quality at the operating point's cost (envelope), the point's paired quality difference from it (difference) with its percentile 95% interval (low, high), and unread, the share of resamples in which the point costs less than the envelope's cheapest corner (Amendment A9, items 12 and 15)
units.mcnemar: per router, task, mix and target: McNemar's test of the operating point against A within the task (b: items only the point gets right; c: only A; p: exact, two-sided); null where the point falls back to A
units.diagnostics: "diagnostic, dev only": none is a policy, selects a setting or threshold, enters the operating-points file or runs on test
units.within_task_concordance: per router and config: pooled over pairs within a task (G and G+ are each one model, so cells are the task alone), ties half, with its paired 95% interval (value, low, high; `undefined`, the share of resamples with no pair, left out), and per task with A7 item 2's warning; size is the number of pairs
units.concordance_differences: `G+ less G`, per config, paired over the same resamples: what our labels add
units.router_score_quantiles: each router's dev router scores per config at the quantiles 0, 5, 25, 50, 75, 95 and 100%; they read no outcome
units.latency: dev, in seconds, per router: the successful attempt's median and p90 (numpy's linear percentile) over calls, per task, with the first call and every reconnect apart and the retries and failed attempts as counts (A15 item 10). It depends on the machine and the network and is quoted as measured
units.latency_conditions: where and when the dev latency was timed (A15 item 10; A16 item 3): the machine and network that hold the stored records, read when this table is built, and the earliest and latest `collected_at` stamp of the dev calls, from the stored records. No network name or address is recorded
units.dev_calls: the server `Date` header of each router's first dev call and the earlier of the two (first_call_server_date), as A15 item 20 records it

comparisons.description: descriptive, with no multiplicity correction: at 95%, about one interval in twenty excludes 0 by chance
